text: The back panel comes away with a screwdriver.
The back panel slides out as soon as the clips are released.
The next bit is the back panel: the screws along the top edge come out first.
The back panel is removed by undoing the screws along the bottom.
Two clips keep the back panel in place, and they let go with a firm push.
A spanner undoes the four screws on the side panel.
Four screws hold the side panel; they come out anticlockwise.
Most people simply lift the side panel away.
Once the screws are out, the side panel is lifted clear.
What happens next is that the side panel comes off.
The boiler casing is removed by undoing the screws along the bottom.
Two clips keep the boiler casing in place, and they let go with a firm push.
Engineers just pull the boiler casing forward until it comes free.
The boiler casing lifts off once the two screws are out.
The next bit is the boiler casing: the screws along the top edge come out first.
Once the screws are out, the front cover of the boiler is lifted clear.
What happens next is that the front cover of the boiler comes off.
The front cover of the boiler comes away with a Allen key.
The front cover of the boiler slides out as soon as the clips are released.
Most people simply lift the front cover of the boiler away.
The control board lifts off once the two screws are out.
The next bit is the control board: the screws along the top edge come out first.
A screwdriver undoes the four screws on the control board.
Four screws hold the control board; they come out anticlockwise.
Engineers just pull the control board forward until it comes free.
The consumer unit cover slides out as soon as the clips are released.
Most people simply lift the consumer unit cover away.
The consumer unit cover is removed by undoing the screws along the bottom.
Two clips keep the consumer unit cover in place, and they let go with a firm push.
The consumer unit cover comes away with a screwdriver.
Four screws hold the socket faceplate; they come out anticlockwise.
Engineers just pull the socket faceplate forward until it comes free.
Once the screws are out, the socket faceplate is lifted clear.
What happens next is that the socket faceplate comes off.
A spanner undoes the four screws on the socket faceplate.
Two clips keep the clamp on the flue joint in place, and they let go with a firm push.
The clamp on the flue joint comes away with a spanner.
The clamp on the flue joint lifts off once the two screws are out.
The next bit is the clamp on the flue joint: the screws along the top edge come out first.
The clamp on the flue joint is removed by undoing the screws along the bottom.
What happens next is that the gas hose on the hob comes off.
A flat blade undoes the four screws on the gas hose on the hob.
The gas hose on the hob slides out as soon as the clips are released.
Most people simply lift the gas hose on the hob away.
Once the screws are out, the gas hose on the hob is lifted clear.
The next bit is the terminal block cover: the screws along the top edge come out first.
The terminal block cover is removed by undoing the screws along the bottom.
Four screws hold the terminal block cover; they come out anticlockwise.
Engineers just pull the terminal block cover forward until it comes free.
The terminal block cover lifts off once the two screws are out.
